How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

   MINUTES OF MARCH 4, 2024
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Vice Chair Duong called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at
6:34 P.M. on Monday, March 4, 2024, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at
City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Barrantes.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Davis Barrantes, Cheryl Anne Cabot, Nancy Duong,
  Theresa Huerta, and Ting Xie

Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Manager Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit comments and
how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services Commission,
email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  MARCH 4, 2024
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot seconded by Commissioner
  Huerta, to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission
  Meeting for February 5, 2024.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-1 as follows:

  AYES:  BARRANTES, CABOT, DUONG, HUERTA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  XIE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  A. INTRODUCTION OF NEW STAFF – ANDY SHOUP

  Manager Morales-Stevens made the introduction.

  The Commission welcomed new Recreation Supervisor, Andy Shoup

  Public Comment: None

  B. DEVELOPMENT OF 2024 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Presented by Manager Morales-Stevens.

  The Commission reviewed and agreed that all the new programs that have been
  added to the workplan are good projects to work on. The Commission also
  agreed to select two commissioners as a committee to serve as liaison for
  events that the City Council has requested to be expanded and added.

  The Commission inquired about the Volunteer Translation Program, and
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the update on the positive outcome of the
  program and the areas that will need improvement. Chair Xie would like to
  provide more assistance to the program improvement.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Huerta seconded by Commissioner
  Cabot, to approve the 2024 Annual Workplan with changes that will be made.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 5-0-0 as follows:

  AYES:  BARRANTES, CABOT, DUONG, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  MARCH 4, 2024
   ABSTAIN:  NONE

  Public Comment: None

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Cabot announced that she will not be continuing to serve on the
  Community Services Commission once her current term expires, after her service
  for the last three terms. She enjoyed her time tremendously helping the
  community with different projects, working with the commission, and having
  many different experiences.

  Commissioner Barrantes inquired about the Farmers Market program and
  would like to get an update once more information becomes available.

  Commissioner Huerta announced she will not be continuing to serve on the
  Community Services Commission once her term expires. Throughout her time
  as a Community Services commissioner, she had had great interaction with the
  community and had a variety of experiences. She’s looking forward to new ideas
  and more suggestions from the new commissioners.

  Commissioner Huerta mentioned parking issues that arose during the Lunar
  Lantern Festival. She did not attend the event, but the event caused a parking
  conflict at San Gabriel Mission because there was also an event going on at the
  church. The commissioner requested that more signs and parking instructions
  be provided for future events to avoid parking confusion, and she will make sure
  that these will also be provided by the church. The commissioner also provided
  an update that San Gabriel Mission church is excited to be welcoming fourteen
  new priests from different countries such as Nigeria, Kenya, India, Bolivia,
  Guatemala, Mexico, and Tonga. The Commissioner felt that it was such a great
  honor that San Gabriel was chosen to be their home.

  Vice Chair Duong expressed her appreciation to both Commissioner Cabot and
  Commissioner Huerta for their contribution to all the projects for the
  Community Services Commission for the last six years. She looks forward to
  seeing and helping at various coming events. Vice Chair Duong attended
  Camilia Fest at Temple City on February 24 and was able to find many affordable
  food options. She’s hoping that more affordable food options will also be
  provided at City of San Gabriel’s events.

  Chair Xie expressed her appreciation to both Commissioner Cabot and
  Commissioner Huerta for serving the Community Services Commission, and she
COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  MARCH 4, 2024
   was able to learn a lot from both commissioners. Chair Xie went to the Mission
  Museum and was able to meet a nice and friendly worker at the bookstore. She
  appreciated that there were different business advertisements at the church.
  Chair Xie also provided a comment on Lunar Lantern Festival that she hoped to
  see more parking instruction or guide provided for future events.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  April 1, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  2024 Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2024 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting. The draft for 2024 outlined in this report
includes items from the 2023 workplan and the amendments made at the November 6,
2023 and February 5, 2024 commission meetings. The Community Services Commission
approved the workplan at the March 4, 2024 commission meeting.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.
 ANNUAL WORKPLAN 2024
The 2024 Workplan sets forth four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Provide new programs for residents with the age groups, 13-18 and 30-50.
  b. Explore program offerings for persons with disabilities including but not
  limited to swim classes.
  c. Continue offering and expand the internship program for youth to assist
  with translation services.
  d. Serve as a liaison for events that City Council has requested be expanded or
  added. Commission members to provide feedback and support for these
  events.
  i. Staff to provide a layout/ general information to the commission for
  review. Commission to appoint two members to serve as a
  committee and work with staff.
  e. Commission to develop a youth ambassador program, host interviews and
  appoint two non-voting ambassadors to the commission.

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Commissioners to staff the Community Services Department information
  booth at City events.
  b. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.

  3. Embrace and Celebrate Community Diversity
  a. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to
  assist in the development and implementation of events and services
  i. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native
  American Community and interfaith groups

  4. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
 b. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  i. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
c. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  i. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information.
d. Recommend that City Council approve the release of an RFP for a new
  registration software during fiscal year 2024/25.
e. Recommend that City Council approve the addition of a part time case
  manager through a third party provider.
